videos.topic: Why Venus is hotter than Mercury
videos.title: Why Venus is Hotter Than Mercury
videos.script_preview: Mercury directly hugs the Sun's intense furnace. Yet, it is not our hottest planet. That title belongs to Venus, much further out. While airless Mercury lets solar heat instantly escape back into the void, Venus is wrapped in a crushing atmosphere ninety-three times heavier than Earth's. Strangely, Venus's thick sulfuric acid clouds reflect eighty percent of incoming sunlight back into space. Only ten percent of the Sun's radiation reaches the rocky surface. videos.title: Why Astronauts Never Stop Falling
videos.script_preview: Why do astronauts float in space? It is not because gravity has disappeared. At the altitude of the Space Station, Earth's gravity is still strongly pulling everything down. In fact, the station and everyone inside are in a non-stop plunge toward the ground. But they never crash, because they are also moving sideways at extreme speeds. As they fall downward, their massive forward velocity curves their path around the planet. The Earth literally curves away beneath them at the exact same rate they fall.
